questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Two major motivations caused me to pick ETH Zürich.
First of all, ETH is a renowned university ranking among the highest in the world. This was a one time opportunity to push myself to the limit and expand my academic knowledge and network. 
Secondly, Switzerland is an incredibly beautiful country. I love mountains, I love skiing, and I love hiking.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. I stayed in a WOKO (student housing office) dorm. They sent a bunch of emails informing me of what to do etc. Likewise, ETH was good at informing me of various events and appointments.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not sure about what is meant by assistance? I handled myself pretty much, I would say.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: As said, I stayed at a WOKO dorm at Meierwiesenstrasse 62. It was fine, but very different from typical danish 'kollegier'. I didn't do much to get the spot - it was offered to me. I did, however, try to search for other housing opportunities, but that proved to be very difficult - at least if you wanted something in Zürich/Campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transport is great and efficient. Living off-campus means that you are likely more connected to the city, since ETH Hönggerberg (my campus) lies up on a big hill in the outskirts of the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The kitchen in Meierwiesenstrasse 62 is a mouthful. If you plan on staying there, then prepare yourself for the worst. But the people are super friendly, and I believe that it is the biggest and most international student housing in Zürich.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember it. It wasn't that difficult. I would say that if you are afraid of how difficult the registration process is, then ETH might be too tough for you. (joke)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The mails I received from ETH were clear and well formulated, and the exchange office at ETH were quick at responding to emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. Smooth sailing. I had spent a lot of time looking through the course catalog before I arrived, so I knew more or less which classes to enroll in

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: don't worry about it. If anything confuses you then write an email to the ETH exchange office and they will help you

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super interesting courses! However the teachers were not all quite as good as I had hoped for.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Pretty difficult. I spend the last couple of my summer vacation preparing for my courses at ETH. But in general, everyone in the auditorium thinks that it is difficult, you are not alone.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
Not as pedagogical. Not quite as intuitive. Not as much focus on 'regneøvelser' and working with the material yourself. Just attending the lectures is not enough to pass - you have to invest a lot of time in understanding the material. 
A similarity between UCPH and ETH is that the lecturers ask question to the students during the lecture. There is a bit of interaction, which is nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Experimental Foundations of Particle Physics ('Semester Project' - not visible in the Course Catalog)
Phenomenology of Particle Physics 1
Neutrino Physics
Symmetries in Physics
Nuclear Energy Conversion

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you are interested in experimental particle physics then: 
Experimental Foundations of Particle Physics ('Semester Project' - not visible in the Course Catalog)
Phenomenology of Particle Physics 1
Neutrino Physics

If you are interested in more theoretical physics then:
Symmetries in Physics (but I also heard from others that the GR and QFT courses are good)

If you are want to try some light engineering: 
Nuclear Energy Conversion

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: When you register at the registration office you have to pay some 50CHF.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Zürich is a very expensive city in general. Food at restaurants/kebab joints/cafeterias etc. were way more expensive than in copenhagen. Groceries were more or less the same, however meat is more expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a free fitness center and bunch of sports activites you can sign up for. I also attended a dance class with my friends (cost 60 CHF for one month), it was super fun. I also spend attended a couple of TTRPG (DnD) events in the local 'Student Fantasy Association'. In general, there are a bunch of offers for fun stuff to do besides studying.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: stated above

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Tanzquotient! (Dancing classes). Dancing is fun and then you are well prepared for the Polyball (enormous gala party in the old main building)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the mountains!!!! My top 3 recommendations are:
1. Oeschinensee (very crowded, but very beautiful)
2. Eggishorn (expert level hike, you feel like invincible once you've reached the top. View to Aletschgletscher, Matterhorn, and Mont Blanc)
3. Churfirsten, Chäserrug (very beautiful view over Walensee, the Churfirsten are legendary)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: pretty easy. My greatest difficulty adjusting was to get used to swiss people blowing their nose very loudly in the middle of a lecture (come to think of it, i never got used to it)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Swiss people are not gonna say hi to you, so you have to say hi to them. Attend some of the many social student events

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Swiss people are not that different from us. But they are more formal.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The effectivity. Both when it comes to public transport and when it comes to answering emails

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. enjoy the privilege it is to study at one of the world's best universities
2. enjoy the mountains
3. when life seems tough, have an Appenzeller Quöllfrisch (beer) with your friends and share your distress with them

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: if you are unsure which courses to enroll in, then know that the first week of the semester is not binding - you can enroll in a course, and if you find out after the first lecture that is not something for you anyway, then there is always the option to drop it and enroll in some other course

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned a lot about particle physics, got some good connections in the field, and even got a reference letter from an ETH professor to apply for the CERN Summer Student programme.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Symmetries in Physics. That course nearly broke me.... but I like to tell myself that i've gained a lot from it

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
